intro.t: Samuel, Saul, and the rise of David.
b: Israel demands a king like the other nations and gets exactly what it asked for. Saul looks the part and is hollow; David is overlooked and is not. The book's most repeated theme is that God does not see as people see.
The relationship between Saul and David is one of the most psychologically acute portraits in ancient literature.

3.h: Speak, for your servant is listening
3.t: The word of the LORD was rare in those days. Samuel does not recognise the voice and has to be told what to say.

8.t: God tells Samuel it is himself they are rejecting, then grants the request with a warning about what kings take. Both halves matter.

16.h: Man looks at the outward appearance
16.t: Spoken while Samuel is admiring Eliab. The LORD looks at the heart.

17.t: Read it as a story about God rather than about courage — David's speech in verses 45 to 47 makes the point explicitly.
David's speech is the interpretation of the whole story: the battle is the LORD's.

2.t: Mary's Magnificat draws on it heavily — the proud scattered, the hungry filled, the barren given children.

15.h: To obey is better than sacrifice
15.t: Samuel's verdict on Saul. The chapter is hard reading and the command in it is among the most difficult in Scripture; the verdict on partial obedience is the part that carries forward. Worth talking through with a pastor or a mature Christian you trust.

24.t: He could kill him and does not, because of the anointing. Then his conscience troubles him even for cutting the robe.

1.t: Bitter in soul, praying so intensely that Eli assumes she is drunk. She gives the child back.

13.t: He does not wait the seven days. Samuel's verdict — a man after God's own heart — is about David before David appears.

18.t: He gives David his robe and his weapons, which is a prince handing over the succession. Saul's jealousy starts the same chapter.

28.t: Saul consults the dead, having earlier banned it. The chapter is strange and grim and records his final collapse.

31.t: The men of Jabesh-Gilead recover his body — the town he rescued in chapter 11. A small act of decency closing a bleak book.

4.t: Israel treats the ark as a charm to win battles, and loses both the battle and the ark. God will not be used.

5.t: The Philistine god is found face down before the ark, twice, the second time broken. The ark does its own fighting.

6.t: On a cart pulled by cows that leave their calves — something only God could explain. The men of Beth Shemesh then die for looking inside it.

7.t: Thus far the LORD has helped us. A stone set up after victory, and the root of the hymn line 'here I raise my Ebenezer'.

9.t: Saul goes out to find lost animals and comes back anointed king. God's providence works through an errand.

10.t: Chosen by lot and nowhere to be found. Saul's reluctance looks like humility and turns out to be something else.

11.t: He rescues Jabesh-Gilead and refuses to execute those who opposed him. It is the man he could have remained.

12.h: Far be it from me to sin by failing to pray
12.t: Samuel's farewell. He counts it a sin not to pray for the people who rejected his leadership.

14.t: Jonathan's faith against a garrison, and Saul's foolish vow that nearly gets his own son killed.

19.t: Michal and Jonathan both protect David against their own father.

20.t: Jonathan's covenant with David, at the cost of his own succession. One of the great friendships of Scripture.

21.t: David eats it at Nob. Jesus cites this in defending his disciples on the Sabbath.

22.t: Saul massacres them. David takes responsibility for having caused it — an unusual admission.

23.h: Jonathan helped him find strength in God
23.t: He went to David in the wilderness to encourage him. One sentence describing what a friend is for.

25.t: A woman whose quick wisdom stops David from shedding blood in anger. He thanks God for her, and for being stopped.

26.h: The spear and the water jug
26.t: A second chance to kill Saul, and a second refusal. David will not take by force what God has promised.

27.t: He despairs and flees to the enemy, lying to their king. His years in the wilderness were not all faith.

29.t: The Philistine commanders refuse to let David fight Israel. A providential rejection saves him from an impossible position.

30.h: David strengthened himself in the LORD
30.t: His men are talking of stoning him. What he does first is turn to God.
